required_work: Retire the pre-re-homing thread-event streams: prove by census that no old-spine stream survives in scope, or migrate the residue onto Agentgres admission — WITHOUT recomputing history.
objective: m5-agentgres-durable-event-subscription-successor re-homes the thread-event WRITE path onto canonical Agentgres admission under option (a), fresh-stream-only: new streams admit through expected-head CAS, and an unmigrated old-spine stream is REFUSED rather than read. This record owns what that leaves behind — <state_dir>/events/<sha256(stream)>.jsonl files carrying kernel-minted seq values. M5_THREAD_EVENT_LEGACY_STREAM_MIGRATION_EXIT=0.
falsifiable_claim: The claim fails if migration recomputes or invalidates any historical admission_hash, if a single stream ends up carrying both kernel-minted and Agentgres sequence values, if any read path falls back to legacy JSONL instead of refusing, or if migration machinery is built for a population the census shows to be empty.
selected_profile: The pre-re-homing per-stream JSONL event logs remaining after the write path moves.
current_implementation_evidence:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-02 adopting option (a) and filing this as the named successor, with three BINDING constraints that are this record's contract:
CONSTRAINT 1 — PER-STREAM ATOMICITY. The unit of the authority switch is the STREAM, never the event. No stream ever carries both kernel-minted and Agentgres seq values. This is what keeps the forced call clean: exact.seq replaces kernel seq, and two sequences over one stream would be a second spine by construction.
CONSTRAINT 2 — REFUSAL, NOT FALLBACK. The re-homed path refuses an unmigrated old-spine stream with a typed refusal naming this successor, and never falls back to reading the JSONL. A fallback is dual-read by accident — it is how option (a) decays into option (c) without anyone deciding it. NAMED CONSEQUENCE: with the old writers deleted, pre-existing threads FREEZE — appends to their streams refuse until migrated or discarded. Acceptable because the population is pre-P0 dev/test runtime state.
CONSTRAINT 3 — MIGRATION NEVER RECOMPUTES HISTORY. Old admission_hash values remain valid over their original records forever. Migration mints NEW Agentgres operations that REFERENCE the old records, binding old->new in a migration receipt, so retained evidence keeps resolving after this cut runs.
CLOSURE BY CENSUS IS LEGITIMATE: director-verified 2026-08-02 that admission_hash appears nowhere under docs/evidence/ and that the M4 verifiers run against mkdtempSync data dirs (fresh state per run), so no retained evidence and no regression re-run binds an old-spine stream. This record may therefore close by proving the surviving in-scope population is zero rather than by building replay-migration machinery. Do not build infrastructure for data nobody retains unless the census says otherwise.
in_scope: A census of surviving old-spine streams in scope.
If the census is non-empty: migration that mints new Agentgres operations referencing the old records, with an old->new migration receipt.
Proof that no read path falls back to legacy JSONL.
out_of_scope: Recomputing or invalidating historical admission_hash values.
Building replay-migration machinery for an empty census.
implementation_actions: Run the census and record the number.
Migrate the residue per stream, atomically, if any.
Assert zero read-fallbacks and zero two-authority streams.
positive_proof: The in-scope old-spine population is zero, or every surviving stream switched authority atomically with an old->new migration receipt and its historical hashes still validate.
adversarial_or_fault_proof: Reject a stream carrying two sequence authorities, a read that falls back to legacy JSONL, a recomputed historical admission_hash, and a migration receipt that does not resolve its old record.
compatibility_and_migration: Pre-existing threads freeze until migrated or discarded; that consequence is named at filing rather than discovered, and is acceptable only while the population is pre-P0 dev state.

code_anchors.evidence_scope: the per-stream JSONL log and lock this record retires

remaining_nonclaims: Filing enforces nothing; leftover JSONL remains until this record closes.
rollback_or_stop_rule: Stop if migration would recompute a historical admission_hash, leave a stream with two sequence authorities, or introduce a read fallback; roll back by leaving the streams frozen and unmigrated.
source_provenance: Owner ruling 2026-08-02: adopt (a), reject (c), file (b) now with per-stream atomicity, refusal-not-fallback, and never-recompute-history as binding constraints.

aggregate_disposition.why: Owner ruling 2026-08-02, written at filing rather than deferred: the bypass the event-substrate cut removes is the WRITE path. Once the writers move to canonical Agentgres admission, leftover JSONL is frozen historical data, not a live spine — so retiring it does not gate the M5 exit.
